title: Progeni predicts candidate melanoma and colorectal-cancer targets validated in cell models
summary: Progeni combines a probabilistic knowledge graph with graph neural networks to rank disease-associated molecular targets. The authors selected six candidates lacking literature support and reported that knockdown of HSP90AB1 and MME reduced proliferation in a murine melanoma line, while knockdown of ADCY5, ADRA2A and EEF2 reduced proliferation in a murine colorectal-cancer line.
ai_technology: Progeni probabilistic knowledge graph and graph neural network
organization: Tsinghua University; Westlake University; Jilin University; Silexon AI Technology

evidence.tested: The authors selected six candidates lacking literature support and reported that knockdown of HSP90AB1 and MME reduced proliferation in a murine melanoma line, while knockdown of ADCY5, ADRA2A and EEF2 reduced proliferation in a murine colorectal-cancer line.
evidence.unknown: The functional validations were in B16F10 and MC38 murine cell lines, not human tumor samples or clinical settings. The paper evaluates a model and validates selected candidates; it does not establish these as clinically effective therapeutic targets.
evidence.ai_role: The graph neural network ranked new target hypotheses from heterogeneous biological networks and literature co-occurrence evidence. Researchers then tested selected predictions by shRNA knockdown in representative murine cancer cell lines.
